event_name: Hissing at Hyde
blurb:
Hyde Farm wraps up the week with something a little different: Hissing at Hyde, a family-friendly event celebrating National Parks and Recreation Month with a focus on the natural world right in your backyard.

The name is a hint at what's coming, reptiles, insects, and the kinds of creatures that make a lot of people jump back and squeal. Which is exactly what makes it fun. It runs Wednesday morning from 10 to noon, which makes it a solid option if you've got younger kids home for the summer or grandkids visiting for the week.

Hyde Farm is one of those East Cobb gems that doesn't get nearly enough attention. This is a good excuse to finally get over there.
scoring_notes: The East Cobb audience skews toward teens and college-age kids, which limits the family-with-young-children fit slightly. However, the grandparent-grandchild angle works well for empty nesters, and the event is directly in the coverage area. Free, low-commitment, and local. Hissing at Hyde has a memorable name that makes it easy to write about engagingly.

event_name: Music on the Hill: Nashville Nation
blurb:
Friday night, free concert, ten minutes from home. That's the whole pitch, and honestly it's a good one.

Music on the Hill brings Nashville Nation to the lawn at Roswell City Hall this Friday as part of their summer concert series. It's an outdoor show, it's country-leaning, and it runs 7 to 9pm, which means you're home at a reasonable hour or you're heading somewhere else after. Either way works.

Bring a blanket or a lawn chair, grab food nearby, and enjoy the fact that you live somewhere with this kind of thing happening on a random Friday night in July. Free doesn't always mean worth it, but this one is.
scoring_notes: This is a recurring monthly series, which limits its uniqueness score. However, each month has a different act and Nashville Nation is a solid draw for the country-friendly East Cobb audience. Free outdoor concerts on a Friday are highly shareable and easy to attend for this demographic. The Roswell City Hall lawn is close to East Cobb and well-known to locals.

event_name: Hyde Farm Walking History Tour
blurb:
Hyde Farm sits right here in East Cobb, and a lot of people drive past it without ever really knowing what's there.

This Saturday morning, Cobb County is running a guided walking history tour of Hyde Farm Park, a one-hour look at the property's history and the land itself. It starts at 10am and wraps by 11, so you're back home before lunch with time to spare. No gear required, no serious hiking involved, just a leisurely walk with some actual context about a place that's been part of this community for a long time.

This is a good one to do with a parent who's visiting, a teenager who needs to get off their phone, or honestly just for yourself if you've been meaning to explore the park. It fills up, so check the Cobb County events page and register ahead of time.
scoring_notes: Hyde Farm is directly in the East Cobb coverage area, which makes this highly relevant geographically. The format (guided tour, one hour, Saturday morning) fits the established-family and empty-nester demo very well. The free price point and low time commitment reduce friction. History and local heritage content resonates strongly with the 65% college-educated, homeowner-heavy audience.

event_name: Big Chicken Chorus 40th Anniversary Show
venue: Lassiter High School Concert Hall, Marietta
blurb:
Forty years is worth showing up for.

The Big Chicken Chorus, one of Marietta's longest-running performing groups, celebrates its 40th anniversary this Sunday afternoon at Lassiter High School's Concert Hall. The show is built around the theme "A Day in the Life of a Big Chicken Barberhopper," with featured performances from local quartets Classic Cuts, Fourmation, and Avoid the Frogs. Yes, that's a real quartet name and yes, they are a ladies' group, which makes this more interesting than your average barbershop night.

Four decades of keeping four-part harmony alive in a community is genuinely something. If you've never actually seen a barbershop performance up close, this is a low-pressure Sunday afternoon to find out what all the fuss is about. The Concert Hall at Lassiter seats a crowd, and this one will fill up with people who've been watching this group for years.
scoring_notes: A 40th anniversary show is a genuinely rare event and earns high uniqueness marks. Lassiter High School is deeply familiar to East Cobb families. The demographic fit is strong for the older end of the audience (empty nesters, longtime Marietta residents). Slightly lower audience match for younger families, but the local connection and milestone nature of the event make it highly shareable and community-relevant.

event_name: Murder Mystery Co. Dinner Theater Show
blurb:
If your Saturday nights have started to blur together, here's something that fixes that.

The Murder Mystery Co. brings their interactive dinner theater show to the Hudson Grille in Kennesaw Saturday evening, and the format is exactly what makes it work for a group: you get a three-course meal, a cast of suspects weaving through the room, and a whodunit to solve before dessert. You can play detective, play a suspect, or just play along from your table while everyone else does the heavy lifting. Either way, nobody's staring at their phone.

This is one of those nights that's genuinely better with more people. Grab another couple, drag your college kid home for the weekend, or finally use it as an excuse to plan that group dinner that's been on the calendar for three months. Call the box office directly at 888-659-2952 and you'll save $9 on fees per ticket.
scoring_notes: Interactive dinner theater is a strong fit for the established-families-and-empty-nesters mix. The format works equally well for couples nights out and multi-generational groups. The Hudson Grille is a recognizable venue name for Cobb County residents. The phone-booking discount is a genuine tangible tip that adds value. Monthly series but each show has a different theme.

event_name: Sunset Sips: Cody Bolden & The Roadhands
blurb:
Thursday night doesn't have to mean sitting on the couch. The Chattahoochee Nature Center kicks off its Sunset Sips series with Cody Bolden & The Roadhands, an Atlanta-based country band whose sound sits right at the intersection of traditional ballads, classic country, and honky tonk. Think real country music, not whatever's on the radio right now.

The setup is exactly what it sounds like: gorgeous views of the property at golden hour, drinks in hand, music on the Great Lawn and covered pavilion. Cody Bolden and his crew are actively touring the U.S. right now, so this is a legitimate act, not a local cover band running through the greatest hits.

If you've driven past the Nature Center a hundred times and never actually stopped, this is the night to fix that. Grab your person, get there by six, and let the week go.
scoring_notes: Sunset Sips is a recurring series, but each show features a different act, and Thursday evening events are high-value for the East Cobb audience because they're easy to commit to without rearranging a weekend. The Chattahoochee Nature Center is literally in the coverage area (Roswell/East Cobb border). Outdoor drinks + live country music is a perfect match for the 40s median-age, established-family-and-empty-nester crowd. Accessible price point, low friction, strong setting.

event_name: Jukebox Giants: Disco Fever!
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
If you grew up with Donna Summer on the radio and ABBA playing at every school dance, this one is going to hit different.

Jukebox Giants: Disco Fever! rolls into the Strand Theatre Friday night with a full cast of singers, dancers, and a live band running through the biggest chart-toppers of the disco era. Bee Gees, ABBA, Donna Summer, all the classics, staged with glittering costumes and choreography that turns the whole room into something close to Studio 54. The median age of this audience is probably going to be right in the sweet spot for genuine nostalgia, not the ironic kind.

The Strand is one of the best small venues in the metro area for a night like this. The room is intimate enough that you actually feel the energy from the stage. Grab dinner on the Square before the show and make a full night of it. Tickets will go, so don't sit on this one.
scoring_notes: Median age of 42 means this audience was kids and teens during the late disco era, which is prime nostalgia territory. The Strand is a familiar, beloved venue for East Cobb residents. Live band and full theatrical production elevates this above a typical cover show. Friday night timing is ideal. Strong demographic and uniqueness fit.

event_name: Music on the Hill: The M-80s (Explosive '80s Rock)
blurb:
Free outdoor concert on the lawn at Roswell City Hall Friday night, and this month it's The M-80s doing straight-up '80s rock for two hours.

This is the July edition of Music on the Hill, a monthly outdoor series that runs May through September. It's a no-fuss Friday night. Bring a blanket or a chair, grab food nearby before you go, and show up around 7:30 to get a good spot before it fills in. The Roswell City Hall lawn is a genuinely nice setting for this, right in the middle of the Historic District.

Starts at 8pm, runs until 10. No tickets, no cover, no reason not to go.
scoring_notes: Free, casual, outdoor concert with an '80s rock theme hits the right notes for the 35-50 age range in this audience. Roswell is right in the coverage zone. The recurring monthly format is a slight knock on uniqueness, but it's the July installment of a specific series, and the '80s rock band concept gives it a distinct identity within the series. Solid Friday night option that's easy to recommend.

event_name: Disney Princess Summer Movies: Beauty and the Beast (1991)
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
If you've got young kids and you're looking for a summer morning that doesn't involve a screen at home, the Strand has a good one on Wednesday.

Beauty and the Beast, the original 1991 version, on the big screen at the Strand, with a Disney Princess meet-and-greet in the lobby before the show. Doors open an hour early so the kids can get photos with real-life princesses before the lights go down. For the 2:30pm showing, there's also a live pre-show concert on the Strand's Mighty Allen Theatre Organ, which is worth experiencing just for the novelty of seeing a real pipe organ perform in a movie house.

Check the Strand's website for tickets and full showtime details. This one is clearly built for families with young children, and it's a genuinely well-executed version of the summer movie experience.
scoring_notes: Young families are a meaningful segment of the Perimeter audience, and a Disney classic with a live princess meet-and-greet is a strong pull for parents with kids under 10. The Strand adds a sense of occasion that a home streaming night doesn't have. Part of a recurring summer series, which knocks uniqueness slightly. The organ pre-show at the 2:30pm showing is a nice differentiator worth calling out.

event_name: Jukebox Giants: Disco Fever!
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
Disco Fever kicks off at the Strand on Friday, and if you're looking for a reason to make it a real night out this weekend, this is it.

Jukebox Giants is a live concert experience built around the biggest disco hits you already know every word to. The Strand is one of the best small venues in the metro area, and a show like this in a room that size hits completely differently than an outdoor festival or a stadium floor. You're close, the sound is great, and the energy in the room actually builds.

Check the Strand's website for showtimes and ticket info. These shows have a tendency to fill up faster than people expect, so don't wait until Friday afternoon to think about it.
scoring_notes: Disco nostalgia skews toward the older end of the Perimeter audience (late 30s through empty nesters), which is a reasonable fit. The Strand is a credible, well-regarded venue that adds legitimacy. Date is right at the start of the newsletter window (Friday July 10). The summary was thin on details, so some specifics on price and time are unavailable, which limits the blurb somewhat. Still a real, specific event worth including.

event_name: Pokémon GO Fest Global Community Celebration at The Battery Atlanta
blurb:
If you've got kids who play Pokémon GO, or honestly if you play it yourself and aren't quite ready to admit that, Saturday at The Battery is worth showing up for.

This is the local celebration of GO Fest 2026: Global, and it's structured as a real community event, not just a reason to walk around a parking lot staring at your phone. There will be Mega Mewtwo Raid Battles, featured Pokémon encounters, and special giveaways, all free, all day from 10am to 7pm. The Battery is already a great place to spend a Saturday, and this gives you an easy, built-in reason to be there with the kids (or the squad).

No tickets, no registration. Just show up, charge your phone the night before, and go find your community.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the young families and young professionals in the Perimeter audience. Pokémon GO skews millennial, which maps well here. Free price removes any friction. The Battery is a familiar, well-loved venue. It's a global event, so it happens in many cities simultaneously, which dials back the uniqueness slightly, but the local gathering format and Mega Mewtwo raids give it a specific, time-limited hook.

event_name: LOVE, CULTURE & CELEBRATION: Experience a Nigerian Wedding
blurb:
Switzer Library is hosting something genuinely different on July 22: a guided cultural experience built around the traditions, dress, food, and ceremony of a Nigerian Igbo wedding.

This is the kind of event that sounds like it's for kids but is really for adults who are curious and want to actually learn something. The metro Atlanta Nigerian community is one of the largest and most established in the country, and a deep dive into the ceremony traditions, the fabrics, the music, and the meaning behind it all is a two-hour afternoon well spent.

Free, no registration required. Runs from 1 to 3pm at Switzer Library on Roswell Street in Marietta. Worth putting on the calendar.
scoring_notes: Highly educated, culturally curious audience is a strong fit for a multicultural educational event like this. The Igbo Nigerian wedding concept is genuinely unique, not something you see regularly on an events calendar. Library setting and free admission make it low-friction. Weekday/midday timing is a limitation for working professionals, but it's summer and works for empty nesters and remote workers. Uniqueness score is high because this specific event is rare.

event_name: FIFA World Cup Final Watch Party
venue: Roswell City Hall Back Lawn, Roswell
blurb:
The FIFA World Cup Final is July 19, and Roswell City Hall is throwing a free watch party on the back lawn.

This is the actual final. One match, winner takes everything, the biggest soccer audience on the planet watching at the same time. There's something about watching a moment like that with a crowd, outdoors on a summer Sunday afternoon, that you just can't replicate on your own couch. Bring the family, bring a chair, and show up a little early to get a good spot on the lawn.

It runs from 2 to 5pm, no tickets, no cost. Just one of the biggest sporting events in the world with your neighbors.
scoring_notes: The World Cup Final is a once-every-four-years event, which gives it very high uniqueness. The 38-year-old median age in this audience skews toward people who follow international soccer, and young families and young professionals both have strong overlap with soccer culture. Free outdoor format is low-friction. Roswell is right in the coverage zone. The community watch party format adds social energy that makes this more than just a sports broadcast.

event_name: Scene on the Green: The Tempest (Shakespeare)
venue: The Art Place at Mountain View, Marietta
blurb:
Free outdoor Shakespeare on a summer Saturday night. That's the pitch, and honestly that pitch does a lot of the work on its own.

Cobb County Parks is putting on The Tempest at The Art Place at Mountain View, and if you haven't been out to this venue for one of their outdoor events, it's worth knowing it's a legitimately beautiful setting. The Tempest is one of Shakespeare's best, magic and shipwrecks and a father trying to hold everything together on a remote island, and it tracks well for a general audience even if you haven't read it in a while.

Bring a blanket, bring snacks, and get there before 7 to stake out a good spot on the lawn. Showtime is 7pm, runs until 10:30. No tickets, no cost. Just a summer night and a really good play.
scoring_notes: 70% college-educated audience is a strong fit for outdoor Shakespeare. Free price and casual outdoor format makes it accessible without feeling lowbrow. Evening timing is better for the adult and empty nester segments. A live Shakespeare production under the stars is genuinely more unique than a generic concert. Great demographic fit for the Perimeter reader.

event_name: Metro Montage XXVI Opening Reception
venue: Marietta Cobb Museum of Art, Marietta
blurb:
This is the 26th year of Metro Montage, one of the only nationwide juried art exhibitions that calls metro Atlanta home, and the opening reception is Saturday night.

Over 800 entries were submitted from across the country. The works on display span oil, sculpture, photography, mixed media, and more, all selected by jurors specifically for the range of skill and vision they represent. This isn't a local craft show. It's a serious, curated exhibition that happens to be walking distance from Marietta Square.

The reception runs from 6 to 8pm. Admission is $10, free for members and exhibiting artists. If you've been meaning to make it out to the museum this summer, this is the night to do it. Good art, good energy, and something to actually talk about afterward.
scoring_notes: Highly educated, higher-income audience maps well to an art museum opening reception. $10 is a non-issue for this demographic. The opening reception format adds a social dimension that an empty-gallery visit doesn't have. A nationwide juried show in its 26th year carries real credibility. Doesn't skew toward families or kids, which is fine for the adult-leaning Perimeter audience.

event_name: Disney Princess Summer Movies: Beauty and the Beast (1991)
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb: The 1991 Beauty and the Beast is one of those films that hits differently in a proper old theater, and the Strand is exactly that kind of venue. The July 15 showing adds a princess meet-and-greet before the film for kids who want the full experience, doors open an hour ahead for photos. For the 2:30pm showing specifically, there's also a live pre-show concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ thirty minutes before the film starts, which is a genuinely cool detail that most movie screenings can't touch. This is a summer Wednesday afternoon well spent, especially if you've got young kids in tow or you're just a person who knows that "Be Our Guest" absolutely slaps and has no shame about it.
scoring_notes: The young families segment of the Perimeter audience is a natural fit here. The Strand Theatre venue adds a layer of charm and legitimacy beyond a typical multiplex. The organ pre-show is a genuinely unique detail. Scores slightly lower than the adult-skewing events because the Perimeter newsletter skews more adult than East Cobb, but the young families presence still makes this worth including.

event_name: Music on the Hill: The M-80s
blurb: Roswell City Hall's lawn turns into a full-on 80s throwback party on July 10 when The M-80s take the stage for Music on the Hill. The drill is simple: spread out a blanket, unpack a picnic, open something cold, and let a band that clearly loves this decade do its job. Big hair anthems, loud guitars, the kind of songs you know every word to even though you'd have a hard time explaining how. This is part of Roswell's America250 summer series, so the energy around it is a little elevated compared to a typical free concert. It's also a Friday night, which makes it an easy first-stop for the evening before deciding where the rest of the night goes.
scoring_notes: Free outdoor concert with a clear 80s nostalgia hook plays well for the 38-median-age Perimeter audience, who grew up in or around that era. The Roswell location is accessible from the Perimeter. Not the most unique event on the list, but the Friday night timing and the picnic-on-the-lawn format make it feel like a solid evening out rather than a detour.

event_name: The Beach Boys at Cobb Energy
venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb: The Beach Boys have been on the road longer than most of their fans have been alive, and in 2026 they're marking the 60th anniversary of Pet Sounds while also celebrating America's 250th. That combination, at Cobb Energy, makes this one worth circling on the calendar. Pet Sounds is widely considered one of the greatest albums ever recorded. "Wouldn't It Be Nice," "God Only Knows," "Sloop John B." You already know the songs. Hearing that catalog live in a real performing arts venue is a different experience than the outdoor festival version. The Perimeter audience skews toward the 35-50 range where nostalgia for this music is real, whether you grew up with it yourself or inherited it from a parent who played it on every road trip. Grab tickets before this one fills up.
scoring_notes: The 60th anniversary of Pet Sounds is a genuine hook that elevates this above a typical touring concert. The Cobb Energy venue is close and familiar to the Perimeter audience. Median age of 38 means the audience has a reasonable connection to this music, though it skews slightly older. Still a strong pick because of the milestone angle and the venue quality.

event_name: Studio Ghibli Fest
blurb: Seven Studio Ghibli films on the big screen, in luxury recliners, over what looks like a multi-day run at Aurora Cineplex in Roswell. If you've never seen Spirited Away or My Neighbor Totoro on a proper theater screen, this is the window. Ghibli films have a visual quality that genuinely looks different at scale, the kind of hand-drawn detail that gets lost on a 55-inch TV. The July 11 screening block runs 5pm to 7pm, which makes it an easy early-evening plan before dinner. The Perimeter crowd has a strong young professional and young family presence, and both groups have Ghibli fans in them. Nostalgia for the adults, discovery for the kids. That's a hard combo to beat.
scoring_notes: Studio Ghibli has broad cross-demographic appeal in an educated, urban-adjacent audience. The luxury recliners angle at Aurora Cineplex makes this feel like a treat rather than just a movie. The 5-7pm window is practical for families and adults alike. Ghibli on the big screen is genuinely rare and worth highlighting.

event_name: Scene on the Green: The Tempest
venue: The Art Place at Mountain View, Marietta
blurb: Free outdoor Shakespeare on a summer night is one of those things that sounds like a lot until you actually show up and realize it's just a great evening. Cobb County Parks is putting on The Tempest at The Art Place at Mountain View, and the setup is exactly what you want: bring your blanket, find a spot on the lawn, and watch magic, romance, and a shipwreck play out under the stars. The Tempest is one of Shakespeare's best for an outdoor setting too. It's a story literally set on an island with storms and sorcery and a cast of characters you don't need a lit degree to enjoy. Three and a half hours of runtime means you're not rushing home. Pack a cooler, get there a little early to settle in, and let the night do its thing.
scoring_notes: An educated adult audience (70% bachelor's degree or higher) is the natural home for free outdoor Shakespeare. The adult-skewing Perimeter demographic fits this better than a family-heavy audience would. Free admission removes any price friction entirely. The Tempest is a strong selection for outdoor performance. Good uniqueness score because live outdoor theater is genuinely less common than a concert or movie night.

event_name: Dunwoody 4th of July Parade
blurb: It's the 4th of July and Dunwoody is doing it the right way. The parade steps off at 9am from the intersection of Mount Vernon Road and Jett Ferry Road, winds 2.7 miles west down Mt. Vernon, through Dunwoody Village, and wraps up with a festival area on the Walgreens side of Dunwoody Village Pkwy. The whole route takes about an hour to walk, so you've got time to grab a coffee first. This one hits different when it's literally in your backyard. No highway, no parking nightmare, no traveling 45 minutes for a fireworks show you've seen a hundred times. Just your neighborhood, a parade, and an excuse to be outside on a holiday morning before the heat fully kicks in. Bring the kids, bring the dog, bring whoever is visiting from out of town.
scoring_notes: The Perimeter audience overlaps heavily with Dunwoody. This is literally a neighborhood event, which gives it a local relevance score other candidates can't match. The mixed family skew of the audience (young families AND young professionals) means a 4th of July parade plays well across the board. It's a recurring annual event, but the 4th of July itself only comes once a year, so the uniqueness dip is minor.

event_name: Moonlight Tours at Truist Park
blurb: You've been to Braves games. You've walked the Battery. But have you ever stood in the dugout after dark with a beer in your hand, looking up at the stars from the same spot where the roster runs out before a first pitch? That's the pitch for this one. Moonlight Tours at Truist Park put you behind the scenes of one of baseball's newest ballparks with a guide, a press box stop, and a cold Blue Moon waiting for you at the Blue Moon Brewery where the tour kicks off. The brewery piece isn't a gimmick either. You get an actual walkthrough of the brewing process from a Molson Coors insider before the ballpark portion starts. The event description says it only comes around "once in a Blue Moon" and look, they're not wrong. This is a genuinely different way to experience a venue you've probably driven past a hundred times. Must be 21+ to drink, but non-alcoholic options are available.
scoring_notes: Adult-skewing audience with disposable income and proximity to Truist Park makes this a natural fit. The behind-the-scenes ballpark angle is genuinely unique. Not a game night, not a concert, not a Battery restaurant visit. It's a totally different experience at a venue the Perimeter audience already has a relationship with. Strong uniqueness score.

event_name: Mezcal Pairing Dinner at Maya Speaktiki
blurb: This is not your standard dinner out. Maya Speaktiki is teaming up with Saca Espantos Mezcal Artesanal for a four-course pairing dinner built around one of the most interesting spirits in the game right now. Each course gets matched to a different expression of the mezcal, which means by the end of the night you've basically taken a guided tour through what artesanal mezcal actually tastes like when it's paired with food that was designed around it. It's the kind of thing that sounds fancy but feels genuinely fun, especially if you've always been curious about mezcal but never had someone walk you through it properly. One night, one restaurant, one mezcal brand. After this one's gone, it's gone.
scoring_notes: Perimeter audience skews adult, educated, and has the income to treat a ticketed dinner as a fun night out rather than a budget decision. This is a one-night-only event at a local Dunwoody venue, which makes it hyper-relevant geographically. The mezcal angle is specific and interesting enough to cut through the noise of generic 'dinner events.' Strong fit across all four factors.
